name: 120 everyday conversations
description: 720 dialogue turns, 120 reply challenges and 20 sentence-building patterns with 60 examples.

items.title: First day at work
items.cue: Practise this situation: First day at work. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I'm Kai. I started today.
B: Welcome! I'm Nina. Which team are you joining?
A: The support team. I'm still finding my way around.
B: I sit near them. I can show you the kitchen.
A: Thanks, that would be really helpful.
B: No problem. Come with me.
expressions: finding my way around — learning where things are

challenge.cue: I didn't catch your name.
challenge.model: It's Kai, spelled K-A-I. Nice to meet you.
challenge.followUp: Which team are you on?

items.title: Joining a hobby group
items.cue: Practise this situation: Joining a hobby group. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, is this the photography group?
B: Yes, it is. Is this your first time here?
A: It is. I've only used my phone so far.
B: That's fine. A few of us use phones too.
A: Great. What are we taking pictures of today?
B: We're starting with the buildings outside.
expressions: I'm still learning the basics — I am a beginner

challenge.cue: Have you brought a camera?
challenge.model: Just my phone today. I'm still learning the basics.
challenge.followUp: What do you enjoy photographing?

items.title: Meeting a neighbour
items.cue: Practise this situation: Meeting a neighbour. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I think we've seen each other in the lift.
B: Yes! I live on the fourth floor. I'm Sam.
A: I'm Mei. I moved in last weekend.
B: Welcome. How are you settling in?
A: Pretty well, thanks. It's much quieter than my old place.
B: That's good. Let me know if you need anything.
expressions: How are you settling in? — How is life in your new place?

challenge.cue: Do you know where the recycling bins are?
challenge.model: Not yet. I've only found the general rubbish bins.
challenge.followUp: Could you show me where they are?

items.title: Introducing two friends
items.cue: Practise this situation: Introducing two friends. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Aisha, this is my friend Ben.
B: Hi, Ben. How do you know each other?
A: We used to work together at a bookshop.
B: Oh, nice. Do you still work there?
A: No, I work at a school now.
B: That sounds interesting. What do you do there?
expressions: We used to work together — we worked together in the past

challenge.cue: Sorry, have we met before?
challenge.model: I don't think so, but you might have seen me at the bookshop.
challenge.followUp: Do you go there often?

items.title: Remembering a name
items.cue: Practise this situation: Remembering a name. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi! We met at Daniel's dinner, didn't we?
B: Yes, we did. It's good to see you again.
A: You too. Sorry, could you remind me of your name?
B: Of course. It's Farah.
A: Farah, thank you. How have you been?
B: Pretty good. I've been busy with a new job.
expressions: could you remind me — please tell me again

challenge.cue: I can't remember your name either!
challenge.model: No worries. I'm Leo. There were a lot of people that night.
challenge.followUp: How do you know Daniel?

items.title: Ending a first conversation
items.cue: Practise this situation: Ending a first conversation. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: It was lovely talking to you.
B: You too. I'm glad we finally met.
A: I should get back to my friends.
B: Of course. Enjoy the rest of the evening.
A: Thanks. Maybe I'll see you at the next event.
B: I hope so. Take care!
expressions: I should get back to — I need to return to someone or something

challenge.cue: Before you go, are you coming next week?
challenge.model: I'm not sure yet. I'll check my schedule.
challenge.followUp: Will you be there?

items.title: Talking about the weekend
items.cue: Practise this situation: Talking about the weekend. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: How was your weekend?
B: Good, thanks. I went for a walk by the lake.
A: That sounds nice. Was it busy?
B: Not really. I went quite early.
A: I might try that next weekend.
B: You should. It's peaceful before nine.
expressions: It was nice to slow down — I enjoyed being less busy

challenge.cue: What did you do over the weekend?
challenge.model: I mostly stayed home and cooked. It was nice to slow down.
challenge.followUp: Do you usually go walking on your own?

items.title: A rainy morning
items.cue: Practise this situation: A rainy morning. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: You got caught in the rain too?
B: Yes, just as I got off the bus.
A: Same here. My shoes are still wet.
B: At least it's warm inside.
A: True. I could really use a hot drink.
B: Me too. Shall we get some tea?
expressions: I could really use — I would really like or need

challenge.cue: I actually like rainy weather.
challenge.model: I do too when I'm indoors. It's the wet shoes I don't enjoy.
challenge.followUp: What's your favourite thing to do on a rainy day?

items.title: Discussing a commute
items.cue: Practise this situation: Discussing a commute. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: How do you usually get to work?
B: I take the train and walk from the station.
A: How long does that take?
B: About forty minutes, if everything runs on time.
A: That's similar to my bus journey.
B: Do you listen to anything on the way?
expressions: on the way — during the journey

challenge.cue: My commute takes nearly two hours.
challenge.model: That sounds tiring. Mine is shorter, but it can still feel long.
challenge.followUp: What helps you pass the time?

items.title: Noticing a new haircut
items.cue: Practise this situation: Noticing a new haircut. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: You've had your hair cut! It looks nice.
B: Thanks. I wanted something easier to manage.
A: It really suits you.
B: That's kind of you. I wasn't sure at first.
A: Did you go somewhere nearby?
B: Yes, the salon opposite the supermarket.
expressions: get used to — become familiar or comfortable with

challenge.cue: I'm not sure I like it yet.
challenge.model: It can take a little time to get used to a change.
challenge.followUp: Have you tried styling it a different way?

items.title: Talking about lunch
items.cue: Practise this situation: Talking about lunch. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: That smells good. What are you having?
B: Leftover curry from last night.
A: Did you make it yourself?
B: Yes, but I followed a very simple recipe.
A: Simple recipes are my favourite.
B: I can send it to you if you'd like.
expressions: if you'd like — if you want

challenge.cue: I'm trying to cook more, but I never know what to make.
challenge.model: I usually choose something with a short ingredient list.
challenge.followUp: What kinds of food do you enjoy?

items.title: A quiet person
items.cue: Practise this situation: A quiet person. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Is this seat taken?
B: No, go ahead.
A: Thanks. It's quite busy in here today.
B: Yes, much busier than usual.
A: I'll let you get back to your book.
B: Thanks. Enjoy your coffee.
expressions: I'll leave you to it — I will stop interrupting you

challenge.cue: Sorry, I'm trying to finish this chapter.
challenge.model: Of course. I'll leave you to it.
challenge.followUp: Could I just check whether this chair is free?

items.title: Inviting a friend for lunch
items.cue: Practise this situation: Inviting a friend for lunch. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Are you free for lunch on Saturday?
B: I think so. What did you have in mind?
A: There's a new noodle place near the station.
B: Sounds good. What time were you thinking?
A: Would half past twelve work for you?
B: Yes, let's meet outside at twelve thirty.
expressions: work for you — be convenient for you

challenge.cue: I can only stay for an hour.
challenge.model: That works for me. We can have a quick lunch.
challenge.followUp: Would somewhere near your next appointment be easier?

items.title: Finding another time
items.cue: Practise this situation: Finding another time. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Would you like to see a film on Friday?
B: I'd love to, but I'm working that evening.
A: No problem. How about Sunday afternoon?
B: Sunday works. Is there anything good on?
A: There's a comedy I'd like to see.
B: Send me the details and I'll have a look.
expressions: How about — used to suggest an option

challenge.cue: Sunday is difficult too, I'm afraid.
challenge.model: No worries. We don't have to decide right now.
challenge.followUp: Which day is usually easiest for you?

items.title: Changing an outdoor plan
items.cue: Practise this situation: Changing an outdoor plan. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: The forecast looks wet for our picnic.
B: Yes, I was just thinking about that.
A: Shall we move it indoors?
B: Good idea. We could have lunch at my place.
A: I can bring sandwiches and fruit.
B: Perfect. I'll make some tea.
expressions: Shall we — used to suggest doing something together

challenge.cue: My flat is too small for everyone.
challenge.model: That's okay. We could choose a café instead.
challenge.followUp: Do you know one with enough space?

items.title: Running late
items.cue: Practise this situation: Running late. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I'm sorry. I'm running about fifteen minutes late.
B: Thanks for letting me know. Is everything okay?
A: Yes, the bus is moving very slowly.
B: No rush. I'll get a table inside.
A: Thanks. I'll message you when I'm close.
B: See you soon.
expressions: I'm running late — I will arrive later than planned

challenge.cue: I need to leave in half an hour.
challenge.model: I'm sorry about the delay. We may only have a short time together.
challenge.followUp: Would you prefer to reschedule?

items.title: Confirming a booking
items.cue: Practise this situation: Confirming a booking. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Are we still on for dinner tomorrow?
B: Yes, definitely. I booked a table for seven.
A: Great. Is it the place on King Street?
B: That's right, next to the florist.
A: Perfect. I'll meet you there.
B: See you tomorrow.
expressions: Are we still on for — Is our plan still happening?

challenge.cue: I thought we said seven thirty.
challenge.model: Thanks for checking. The booking is at seven, but I can ask to change it.
challenge.followUp: Which time would you prefer?

items.title: Declining an invitation
items.cue: Practise this situation: Declining an invitation. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Do you want to join us for dinner tonight?
B: Thanks for asking, but I need a quiet evening.
A: Of course. It's been a busy week.
B: It really has. I hope you have a good time.
A: Thanks. Maybe another time.
B: Definitely. Let's catch up next week.
expressions: Thanks for asking, but — a polite way to decline

challenge.cue: Come on, just for an hour!
challenge.model: Thanks, but I'm going to stay home tonight. I need some rest.
challenge.followUp: Could we arrange something next week instead?

items.title: Borrowing a charger
items.cue: Practise this situation: Borrowing a charger. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could I borrow your charger for a few minutes?
B: Sure. What kind of phone do you have?
A: It uses a USB-C cable.
B: This one should work.
A: Thanks. I'll give it back before you leave.
B: No problem. I'm here until four.
expressions: Could I borrow — a polite request to use something temporarily

challenge.cue: I'm using it at the moment.
challenge.model: That's okay. My battery should last a little longer.
challenge.followUp: Could I borrow it when you're finished?

items.title: Carrying something heavy
items.cue: Practise this situation: Carrying something heavy. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: That box looks heavy. Would you like a hand?
B: Yes, please. I can't open the door while holding it.
A: I'll get the door for you.
B: Thanks. Could you hold it open for a moment?
A: Of course. Take your time.
B: That's a big help. Thank you.
expressions: Would you like a hand? — Do you want some help?

challenge.cue: Actually, could you carry the other box?
challenge.model: I can help with the smaller one. The large one is too heavy for me.
challenge.followUp: Where would you like me to put it?

items.title: Asking for directions inside
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for directions inside. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Excuse me, where's the meeting room?
B: Which one are you looking for?
A: The room called Cedar.
B: Go down this corridor and turn left.
A: Thanks. Is it before the stairs?
B: Yes, it's the first door on your right.
expressions: Could you point me towards — Could you show me the direction of

challenge.cue: There are two rooms with similar names.
challenge.model: I see. My invitation says Cedar Two.
challenge.followUp: Could you point me towards that one?

items.title: Asking for a small favour
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for a small favour. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could you water my plants while I'm away?
B: Sure. How long will you be gone?
A: Just four days. They only need watering once.
B: Okay. Could you leave me some instructions?
A: Of course. I'll put a note by the kitchen window.
B: Great. Enjoy your trip.
expressions: Could you leave me — a polite request to provide something

challenge.cue: I'm away for part of that week too.
challenge.model: Thanks for telling me. I'll ask someone else to cover those days.
challenge.followUp: Which days will you be home?

items.title: Offering help without pressure
items.cue: Practise this situation: Offering help without pressure. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: You look busy. Can I help with anything?
B: Thanks, but I've nearly finished.
A: Okay. I'm free for the next ten minutes.
B: Actually, could you check these names?
A: Sure. What should I look for?
B: Just spelling mistakes, please.
expressions: Which part is most urgent? — What needs attention first?

challenge.cue: I need some help, but it will take an hour.
challenge.model: I only have ten minutes now, but I can help with one small part.
challenge.followUp: Which part is most urgent?

items.title: Asking someone to speak quietly
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking someone to speak quietly. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Sorry, could you lower your voice a little?
B: Oh, sorry. I didn't realise I was being loud.
A: No problem. I'm trying to hear this call.
B: Of course. I'll move to the other room.
A: Thanks, I appreciate it.
B: You're welcome.
expressions: Would you mind — a polite request, usually followed by an -ing form

challenge.cue: I can't hear the person on my phone either.
challenge.model: That sounds frustrating. Maybe we could use separate rooms.
challenge.followUp: Would you mind moving to the kitchen?

items.title: Ordering a drink
items.cue: Practise this situation: Ordering a drink. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, could I have a small latte, please?
B: Of course. Is that to have here or take away?
A: To have here, please.
B: Would you like anything to eat?
A: Just the coffee, thanks.
B: That'll be ready at the end of the counter.
expressions: Just the coffee, thanks — politely ordering only that item

challenge.cue: We've run out of regular milk.
challenge.model: Okay. I'll have it with oat milk, please.
challenge.followUp: Is there an extra charge for that?

items.title: Choosing a meal
items.cue: Practise this situation: Choosing a meal. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: What would you recommend?
B: The grilled chicken is popular.
A: Does it come with anything?
B: Yes, rice and a small salad.
A: That sounds good. I'll have that, please.
B: Certainly. Anything to drink?
expressions: Does it come with — Is something included with it?

challenge.cue: The grilled chicken has sold out.
challenge.model: No problem. I'll choose something else.
challenge.followUp: What would you recommend instead?

items.title: Checking ingredients
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking ingredients. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Does this soup contain peanuts?
B: Let me check with the kitchen.
A: Thank you. I have a peanut allergy.
B: The chef says it contains peanut oil.
A: Thanks for checking. I won't order that.
B: I can ask about another dish for you.
expressions: Thanks for checking — showing appreciation for verification

challenge.cue: We can't confirm whether it contains peanuts.
challenge.model: Thanks for being honest. I'll choose something elsewhere.
challenge.followUp: Could you cancel the soup order, please?

items.title: Correcting an order
items.cue: Practise this situation: Correcting an order. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Excuse me, I ordered an iced tea.
B: I'm sorry. Did we bring you a hot one?
A: Yes, this one is hot.
B: I'll replace it for you.
A: Thank you. I appreciate it.
B: Sorry about the mix-up.
expressions: Sorry about the mix-up — apologising for a mistake or confusion

challenge.cue: The iced tea will take another ten minutes.
challenge.model: That's okay. I can wait a little longer.
challenge.followUp: Could I have some water while I wait?

items.title: Sharing dishes
items.cue: Practise this situation: Sharing dishes. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Shall we order a few dishes to share?
B: That sounds good. What do you feel like?
A: Maybe noodles and some vegetables.
B: I'd like some chicken too.
A: Great. Let's start with those three.
B: We can order more if we're still hungry.
expressions: What do you feel like? — What would you enjoy now?

challenge.cue: I don't really feel like sharing today.
challenge.model: That's fine. Let's each choose our own meal.
challenge.followUp: What are you thinking of ordering?

items.title: Paying after a meal
items.cue: Practise this situation: Paying after a meal. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could we have the bill, please?
B: Certainly. Was everything all right?
A: Yes, thank you. We enjoyed it.
B: I'm glad to hear that. Here you are.
A: Can we pay separately?
B: Yes. Tell me which items you had.
expressions: sort it out — resolve or organise something

challenge.cue: We can only take one payment for the table.
challenge.model: Okay, I'll pay this time and we'll sort it out between us.
challenge.followUp: Can I pay by card?

items.title: Finding the right size
items.cue: Practise this situation: Finding the right size. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Do you have this shirt in a medium?
B: Let me check. What colour would you like?
A: The same blue, please.
B: Here you go. Would you like to try it on?
A: Yes, please. Where are the fitting rooms?
B: Just behind the stairs.
expressions: try it on — put on clothing to see whether it fits

challenge.cue: We only have it in black.
challenge.model: I might try the black one, then.
challenge.followUp: Could you show me what it looks like?

items.title: Comparing two products
items.cue: Practise this situation: Comparing two products. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: What's the difference between these two bags?
B: This one is larger and has more pockets.
A: Is the smaller one waterproof?
B: It's water-resistant, but not fully waterproof.
A: I see. I'll need something for heavy rain.
B: Then let me show you another option.
expressions: more than I planned to spend — above my intended budget

challenge.cue: The waterproof one costs quite a bit more.
challenge.model: It's more than I planned to spend. I'll think about it.
challenge.followUp: Do you have a less expensive waterproof option?

items.title: Browsing without buying
items.cue: Practise this situation: Browsing without buying. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, can I help you find anything?
B: I'm just looking for now, thanks.
A: Of course. Let me know if you need a size.
B: I will. These jackets look nice.
A: They're on the rack near the window.
B: Thanks. I'll have a look.
expressions: I'm just looking — I am browsing and do not need help yet

challenge.cue: This offer ends today.
challenge.model: Thanks for letting me know. I still need time to decide.
challenge.followUp: Can I find the product details online?

items.title: Checking a price
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking a price. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Excuse me, how much is this notebook?
B: It's twelve ringgit.
A: Thanks. Does that price include the cover?
B: Yes, the cover comes with it.
A: Great. I'll take one.
B: Would you like a bag?
expressions: I'll take one — I have decided to buy one

challenge.cue: The display price was for a smaller notebook.
challenge.model: Oh, I see. I misunderstood the sign.
challenge.followUp: Could you show me the twelve-ringgit one?

items.title: Exchanging an item
items.cue: Practise this situation: Exchanging an item. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I'd like to exchange this jumper.
B: Is there anything wrong with it?
A: It's too small. I need the next size up.
B: Do you have the receipt?
A: Yes, here it is.
B: Thanks. I'll check what sizes we have.
expressions: the next size up — one size larger

challenge.cue: We don't have the larger size in this colour.
challenge.model: Could I exchange it for a different colour instead?
challenge.followUp: Which colours are available in the larger size?

items.title: Reporting a faulty item
items.cue: Practise this situation: Reporting a faulty item. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I bought these headphones yesterday, but one side doesn't work.
B: I'm sorry to hear that. May I see them?
A: Of course. I've brought the receipt too.
B: Thank you. We'll test them first.
A: That's fine. I'd prefer a replacement if possible.
B: I'll check our replacement options.
expressions: I'd prefer — I would rather choose

challenge.cue: We need to send them away for inspection.
challenge.model: Okay. I'd like to understand what happens next.
challenge.followUp: How long does the inspection usually take?

items.title: Splitting a shared cost
items.cue: Practise this situation: Splitting a shared cost. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: The taxi came to forty ringgit.
B: Okay. There were four of us.
A: So that's ten ringgit each.
B: I'll transfer my share now.
A: Thanks. I'll send you my payment details.
B: Great. Let me know when it arrives.
expressions: my share — the part of a cost that I should pay

challenge.cue: I don't have my banking app with me.
challenge.model: No problem. You can pay me later.
challenge.followUp: Would tomorrow be okay?

items.title: Checking an unfamiliar charge
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking an unfamiliar charge. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I don't recognise this charge on my bill.
B: Could you tell me which charge you mean?
A: The service fee listed below the total.
B: Let me check the details.
A: Thank you. I wasn't expecting that fee.
B: I'll explain what it covers.
expressions: I don't recognise — I do not know or remember this

challenge.cue: I need to transfer you to another team.
challenge.model: Okay. I'd like to keep the details clear.
challenge.followUp: Could you give me a reference number?

items.title: Asking about a subscription
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking about a subscription. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'd like to ask about my monthly plan.
B: Of course. What would you like to know?
A: Can I switch to a cheaper plan?
B: Let me check which plans are available.
A: Thanks. I don't use all my current features.
B: I'll explain the differences.
expressions: switch to — change from one option to another

challenge.cue: The cheaper plan has a lower usage limit.
challenge.model: That might still be enough for me.
challenge.followUp: How much usage does it include?

items.title: Cancelling a service
items.cue: Practise this situation: Cancelling a service. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'd like to cancel my membership, please.
B: May I ask why you're cancelling?
A: I've moved, so I can't use this branch anymore.
B: I understand. Let me check your account.
A: Thank you. Please explain any final charges.
B: Of course. I'll go through them with you.
expressions: go through — explain or examine something step by step

challenge.cue: Would you like to pause it instead?
challenge.model: Thanks, but I'd prefer to cancel because I've moved away.
challenge.followUp: Could you confirm the cancellation date?

items.title: A payment fails
items.cue: Practise this situation: A payment fails. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'm sorry, the payment didn't go through.
B: Oh, let me check my phone.
A: Take your time.
B: It looks like there's a connection problem.
A: You can try again or use another method.
B: I'll use a different card, please.
expressions: didn't go through — did not complete successfully

challenge.cue: It looks as though I've been charged twice.
challenge.model: I can see two notifications on my phone. Could we check before I try again?
challenge.followUp: Which payments can you see on your system?

items.title: Getting a receipt
items.cue: Practise this situation: Getting a receipt. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could I get a receipt for that, please?
B: Certainly. Paper or email?
A: Paper would be great.
B: Here you are.
A: Thanks. Could you include the company name?
B: I'll check whether I can add it.
expressions: Could I get — a polite way to ask for something

challenge.cue: Our printer isn't working.
challenge.model: An email receipt is fine instead.
challenge.followUp: Could you check the email address with me before sending it?

items.title: Buying a train ticket
items.cue: Practise this situation: Buying a train ticket. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: One ticket to Central, please.
B: Single or return?
A: Return, please. Can I come back this evening?
B: Let me show you the ticket options.
A: Thanks. I don't travel this route often.
B: No problem. This screen explains the times.
expressions: I mean — used to clarify your meaning

challenge.cue: There are two stations called Central on this map.
challenge.model: I mean the one near the city library.
challenge.followUp: Could you show me the correct route?

items.title: Checking a bus route
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking a bus route. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Excuse me, does this bus go to the hospital?
B: It stops across the road from it.
A: Great. How many stops is that?
B: About six stops from here.
A: Thank you. I'll watch for it.
B: There's a large sign outside.
expressions: across the road from — on the opposite side of the road

challenge.cue: The route has changed today.
challenge.model: Thanks for telling me. I need to reach the main entrance.
challenge.followUp: Which stop should I use today?

items.title: Finding a pickup point
items.cue: Practise this situation: Finding a pickup point. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I'm outside the shopping centre.
B: Which entrance are you at?
A: The one beside the pharmacy.
B: I'm at the main entrance near the fountain.
A: Okay, I'll walk over there.
B: Thanks. I'll wait by the fountain.
expressions: I'll walk over there — I will walk to that place

challenge.cue: I can't see a pharmacy.
challenge.model: No problem. Let's use a different landmark.
challenge.followUp: Can you see the large fountain?

items.title: Asking for walking directions
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for walking directions. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Excuse me, is the library near here?
B: Yes, it's about a ten-minute walk.
A: Could you tell me how to get there?
B: Go straight, then turn right at the bank.
A: So I turn right after the bank?
B: At the bank, just before the crossing.
expressions: Could you tell me how to — a polite way to ask for instructions

challenge.cue: I'm not very good with street names.
challenge.model: That's okay. Landmarks are easier for me too.
challenge.followUp: What should I look for before I turn?

items.title: Missing a stop
items.cue: Practise this situation: Missing a stop. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I think I've missed my stop.
B: Which stop did you want?
A: The one near the museum.
B: We passed it a few minutes ago.
A: Okay. I'll get off at the next stop.
B: You can check the return route there.
expressions: get off — leave a bus, train or other vehicle

challenge.cue: The next stop is quite far away.
challenge.model: I see. I'll need to adjust my route.
challenge.followUp: Where is the nearest place I can change buses?

items.title: Arranging a lift
items.cue: Practise this situation: Arranging a lift. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could you give me a lift to the station?
B: Sure. What time do you need to be there?
A: By eight, if possible.
B: Let's leave at half past seven.
A: That would be great. I'll be ready.
B: I'll message you when I'm outside.
expressions: give me a lift — take me somewhere in your vehicle

challenge.cue: I can only drop you halfway.
challenge.model: That would still help. I can walk from there.
challenge.followUp: Where would be easiest for you to stop?

items.title: Checking in
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking in. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I have a reservation under Lee.
B: Welcome. Could I see your identification, please?
A: Of course. Here you are.
B: Thank you. You're staying for two nights?
A: That's right. Is breakfast included?
B: Let me check your booking.
expressions: under Lee — booked using the name Lee

challenge.cue: I can't find a booking under that name.
challenge.model: I have the confirmation email here.
challenge.followUp: Could you check the booking reference?

items.title: Arriving before check-in
items.cue: Practise this situation: Arriving before check-in. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, we've arrived a little early.
B: Welcome. Your room isn't ready yet.
A: That's okay. Could we leave our bags here?
B: Certainly. We'll store them for you.
A: Thank you. What time should we come back?
B: Please check with us after two.
expressions: leave our bags here — temporarily store our luggage here

challenge.cue: The room may not be ready until three.
challenge.model: That's fine. We'll explore the area first.
challenge.followUp: Could you call us when it's ready?

items.title: A noisy hotel room
items.cue: Practise this situation: A noisy hotel room. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, there's quite a lot of noise outside my room.
B: I'm sorry about that. Which room are you in?
A: Room 204. I can hear music from downstairs.
B: I'll ask the team to check.
A: Thank you. I have an early start tomorrow.
B: We'll see what we can do.
expressions: I have an early start — I need to begin my day early

challenge.cue: The event won't finish for another hour.
challenge.model: I understand, but I'm having trouble sleeping.
challenge.followUp: Is a quieter room available?

items.title: Asking about local activities
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking about local activities. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: We have a free afternoon. Any suggestions?
B: Do you prefer museums or outdoor activities?
A: Probably something outdoors.
B: There's a nice walking path by the river.
A: That sounds good. Is it easy to reach?
B: Yes, I can show you on the map.
expressions: Any suggestions? — Do you have any ideas?

challenge.cue: The river path is closed today.
challenge.model: Thanks for checking. We'll choose somewhere else.
challenge.followUp: Is there a park nearby instead?

items.title: Storing bags after checkout
items.cue: Practise this situation: Storing bags after checkout. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: We're checking out, but our train isn't until evening.
B: Would you like us to store your bags?
A: Yes, please. That would be helpful.
B: We'll give you a collection tag.
A: Thanks. We'll be back around five.
B: That's fine. Keep the tag with you.
expressions: We'll be back around — we will return at approximately

challenge.cue: The storage area closes at four.
challenge.model: Thanks for letting us know. We'll come back before then.
challenge.followUp: Is three thirty okay?

items.title: Finding a lost item
items.cue: Practise this situation: Finding a lost item. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I think I left my jacket in the room.
B: Which room were you staying in?
A: Room 312. It's a dark green jacket.
B: I'll contact housekeeping.
A: Thank you. I checked out this morning.
B: Could you leave a phone number?
expressions: turns up — is found or appears

challenge.cue: We haven't found it yet.
challenge.model: Thanks for checking. It might be in the wardrobe.
challenge.followUp: Could you let me know if it turns up?

items.title: Sharing housework
items.cue: Practise this situation: Sharing housework. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could we talk about the cleaning this week?
B: Sure. What needs doing?
A: The kitchen and bathroom both need attention.
B: I can clean the bathroom on Saturday.
A: Thanks. I'll take care of the kitchen.
B: Great. Let's get the supplies tomorrow.
expressions: take care of — handle a task or responsibility

challenge.cue: Saturday won't work for me after all.
challenge.model: No problem. We can adjust the plan.
challenge.followUp: Which day would be better?

items.title: Reporting a leak
items.cue: Practise this situation: Reporting a leak. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, there's water dripping under the kitchen sink.
B: When did you first notice it?
A: About ten minutes ago.
B: Thanks for telling me. I'll arrange a repair.
A: Could you let me know when someone can come?
B: Yes, I'll contact the maintenance team now.
expressions: When did you first notice it? — When did you become aware of it?

challenge.cue: The repair person can't come until tomorrow.
challenge.model: Thanks for the update. I'm concerned about the water spreading.
challenge.followUp: What should I do while I wait?

items.title: Receiving a delivery
items.cue: Practise this situation: Receiving a delivery. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I have a parcel for Alex.
B: That's me. Thank you.
A: Could you confirm the flat number?
B: Flat 8, on the second floor.
A: Great. Here's your parcel.
B: Thanks. Have a good day.
expressions: I don't think that's mine — I believe it belongs to someone else

challenge.cue: The name on this parcel is different.
challenge.model: I don't think that's mine. Please check the address.
challenge.followUp: Could it be for another flat?

items.title: Asking a neighbour about noise
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking a neighbour about noise. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, could I ask a quick favour?
B: Of course. What's up?
A: Could you turn the music down after ten?
B: Sorry, I didn't realise you could hear it.
A: Thanks. My bedroom is next to that wall.
B: I'll keep it lower tonight.
expressions: What's up? — informally asking what someone wants or what is happening

challenge.cue: We're having a birthday party tonight.
challenge.model: I understand. I still need to sleep, so a lower volume would help.
challenge.followUp: Could you turn it down after ten?

items.title: Planning groceries
items.cue: Practise this situation: Planning groceries. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'm going to the supermarket. Do we need anything?
B: We're nearly out of rice.
A: Okay. I'll get a bag.
B: Could you get some eggs too?
A: Sure. Anything else?
B: That's everything, thanks.
expressions: We're nearly out of — we have very little left

challenge.cue: I just bought rice this morning.
challenge.model: Great, I'll leave that off the list.
challenge.followUp: Do we still need eggs?

items.title: Hosting a visitor
items.cue: Practise this situation: Hosting a visitor. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Come in! It's good to see you.
B: You too. Thanks for inviting me.
A: Would you like something to drink?
B: Water would be lovely, thanks.
A: Make yourself comfortable. I'll get you a glass.
B: Thanks. You have a lovely place.
expressions: Make yourself comfortable — relax and feel at home

challenge.cue: I can only stay for a short while.
challenge.model: That's fine. I'm glad you could come.
challenge.followUp: Do you have time for a quick drink?

items.title: Booking a haircut
items.cue: Practise this situation: Booking a haircut. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, could I book a haircut for Saturday?
B: Of course. Morning or afternoon?
A: Afternoon would be better.
B: We have a space at two thirty.
A: That works. Could I book that, please?
B: Certainly. What name should I put it under?
expressions: fully booked — no appointments are available

challenge.cue: Saturday is fully booked.
challenge.model: Okay. I can come another day.
challenge.followUp: Do you have anything on Sunday?

items.title: Rescheduling a visit
items.cue: Practise this situation: Rescheduling a visit. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, I need to change my appointment.
B: No problem. When is your current appointment?
A: Tuesday at ten.
B: When would you like to move it to?
A: Would Thursday afternoon be possible?
B: Let me check what's available.
expressions: move it to — change it to a different time or date

challenge.cue: The next available time is the following week.
challenge.model: I see. I'll need to check my calendar.
challenge.followUp: Could you tell me the exact date and time?

items.title: Explaining symptoms to reception
items.cue: Practise this situation: Explaining symptoms to reception. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'd like to make an appointment with a doctor.
B: Certainly. Could you briefly describe the problem?
A: I've had a sore throat for three days.
B: I'll check the available appointments.
A: Thank you. Is there anything this afternoon?
B: Let me look for you.
expressions: I've had ... for — describing how long a condition has continued

challenge.cue: Could you repeat how long you've had it?
challenge.model: It's been three days. It started on Monday.
challenge.followUp: Would you like me to explain any other symptoms?

items.title: Asking a professional to explain
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking a professional to explain. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'm sorry, I didn't understand that term.
B: Of course. Let me explain it another way.
A: Thank you. Simple words would help.
B: Certainly. I'll write down the main points too.
A: That would be useful.
B: Please ask if anything is still unclear.
expressions: Could you explain — a polite request for clearer information

challenge.cue: Which part didn't you understand?
challenge.model: I understood the first part, but not what I need to do next.
challenge.followUp: Could you explain the next step?

items.title: Waiting longer than expected
items.cue: Practise this situation: Waiting longer than expected. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Excuse me, my appointment was at eleven.
B: I'm sorry. We're running behind today.
A: I understand. Do you know roughly how long the wait is?
B: About twenty more minutes.
A: Thanks for the update. I'll wait here.
B: We'll call your name as soon as we're ready.
expressions: running behind — taking longer than planned

challenge.cue: It may be another hour.
challenge.model: Thanks for telling me. I have another commitment later.
challenge.followUp: Could I book a different time?

items.title: Confirming instructions
items.cue: Practise this situation: Confirming instructions. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Just to check, I should bring the original document?
B: Yes, and a copy if you have one.
A: Okay. Do I also need the confirmation email?
B: Yes, please show it at reception.
A: Great. I'll have everything ready.
B: Thank you. See you on Thursday.
expressions: Just to check — introducing a request for confirmation

challenge.cue: The requirements have changed since your last visit.
challenge.model: Thanks for letting me know. I'd like to make sure I bring everything.
challenge.followUp: Could you send me the current list?

items.title: Giving a short update
items.cue: Practise this situation: Giving a short update. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: How's the report coming along?
B: The first draft is finished. I'm checking the figures now.
A: Great. When do you think it'll be ready?
B: I expect to send it by three.
A: Thanks. Let me know if you need anything.
B: Will do. I'll message you when it's sent.
expressions: coming along — progressing

challenge.cue: We need it before lunch now.
challenge.model: I can send the completed sections before lunch, but the figures need more checking.
challenge.followUp: Which sections do you need first?

items.title: Explaining a delay
items.cue: Practise this situation: Explaining a delay. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I wanted to update you on the order.
B: Thanks. Is it ready?
A: Not yet. We're waiting for one missing part.
B: Do you have an estimated arrival date?
A: The supplier says Thursday. I'll confirm when it arrives.
B: Okay. Please keep me posted.
expressions: Please keep me posted — please continue giving me updates

challenge.cue: Thursday is too late for us.
challenge.model: I understand. I'll check whether there's an alternative.
challenge.followUp: Would a partial delivery help?

items.title: Asking for priorities
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for priorities. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I've got two urgent tasks this morning.
B: Which ones?
A: The customer reply and the sales summary.
B: Please finish the customer reply first.
A: Okay. Then I'll work on the summary.
B: Thanks. Let me know if that changes your timing.
expressions: work on — spend time doing or improving something

challenge.cue: Actually, a third task has just come in.
challenge.model: Okay. I'll need to review the order of work.
challenge.followUp: Which of the three should come first?

items.title: Admitting a mistake
items.cue: Practise this situation: Admitting a mistake. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I've spotted a mistake in the file I sent.
B: Thanks for telling me. What happened?
A: I used last week's date in the heading.
B: Can you send a corrected version?
A: Yes. I'll clearly mark it as the updated file.
B: Great. I'll use the new version.
expressions: I've spotted a mistake — I have noticed an error

challenge.cue: I've already forwarded it to the client.
challenge.model: I'm sorry about that. I'll send the corrected file straight away.
challenge.followUp: Would you like me to draft a short explanation?

items.title: Asking for feedback
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for feedback. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could you give me some feedback on this draft?
B: Sure. What would you like me to focus on?
A: Whether the explanation is clear.
B: Okay. The introduction is easy to follow.
A: That's helpful. What about the middle section?
B: I think it needs a concrete example.
expressions: easy to follow — easy to understand

challenge.cue: I haven't had time to read it yet.
challenge.model: No problem. Even a few comments later would help.
challenge.followUp: When would be a good time for me to check back?

items.title: Handing over a task
items.cue: Practise this situation: Handing over a task. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'll be away tomorrow, so here's a quick handover.
B: Thanks. What's still outstanding?
A: One customer is waiting for a delivery date.
B: Where can I find the details?
A: They're in the shared folder under today's date.
B: Got it. I'll check that first.
expressions: still outstanding — not yet completed or resolved

challenge.cue: I don't have access to that folder.
challenge.model: Thanks for flagging that. I'll ask for access to be arranged.
challenge.followUp: Can you open the main shared drive?

items.title: Joining a discussion
items.cue: Practise this situation: Joining a discussion. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could I add something here?
B: Of course. Go ahead.
A: I think we should check the timing with the delivery team.
B: That's a good point.
A: They may need more than two days.
B: Let's ask them before we confirm the date.
expressions: Could I add something? — politely asking to contribute

challenge.cue: We're short on time. Could you be brief?
challenge.model: Of course. My main point is that we need to confirm delivery timing.
challenge.followUp: Can we check that before agreeing on the date?

items.title: Clarifying a task
items.cue: Practise this situation: Clarifying a task. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: When you say 'finish the page', what do you mean?
B: I mean the text and images should be ready.
A: Does that include the mobile layout?
B: Yes, please include that too.
A: Okay. Thanks for clarifying.
B: No problem. Let me know if anything else is unclear.
expressions: When you say ... what do you mean? — asking about intended meaning

challenge.cue: I only meant the first section.
challenge.model: Thanks, that helps. I'll focus on the first section for now.
challenge.followUp: Should I leave the other sections as they are?

items.title: Disagreeing politely
items.cue: Practise this situation: Disagreeing politely. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I think we should send it today.
B: I see your point, but we haven't checked the names yet.
A: That should only take a few minutes.
B: True. Could we check them before sending?
A: Yes, that seems reasonable.
B: Great. I'll do that now.
expressions: I see your point, but — acknowledging a view before disagreeing

challenge.cue: I don't think another check is necessary.
challenge.model: I understand. I'm concerned because two names changed yesterday.
challenge.followUp: Could we at least confirm those two?

items.title: Asking for an example
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for an example. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could you give us an example of the problem?
B: Sure. Yesterday, two people received the same confirmation.
A: Was it sent twice to the same address?
B: No, one message went to the wrong person.
A: I see. That helps me understand.
B: We should check how the addresses are selected.
expressions: Could you give us an example? — asking for a concrete illustration

challenge.cue: I don't have a specific example with me.
challenge.model: That's okay. A real example would help us investigate later.
challenge.followUp: Could you send one when you find it?

items.title: Summarising a decision
items.cue: Practise this situation: Summarising a decision. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: So we've agreed to start with a small trial.
B: Yes, with ten participants.
A: I'll prepare the instructions.
B: And I'll contact the participants.
A: Shall we review the results next Friday?
B: Yes, let's put that in the calendar.
expressions: So we've agreed — summarising a shared decision

challenge.cue: I thought we agreed on twenty participants.
challenge.model: I may have misunderstood. Let's confirm the number now.
challenge.followUp: Are we starting with ten or twenty?

items.title: Asking for thinking time
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for thinking time. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: What do you think of this proposal?
B: I'd like a little time to think it through.
A: Of course. What would help?
B: I'd like to compare the costs first.
A: That's fair. Could you come back to us tomorrow?
B: Yes, I'll send my thoughts in the morning.
expressions: think it through — consider something carefully

challenge.cue: We need a first reaction now.
challenge.model: My first reaction is positive, but I haven't checked the costs yet.
challenge.followUp: Can I confirm my view after reviewing them?

items.title: Starting a phone call
items.cue: Practise this situation: Starting a phone call. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hello, is this the repair centre?
B: Yes, it is. How can I help?
A: I'm calling about a booking I made yesterday.
B: Certainly. Do you have a reference number?
A: Yes, it's R-418.
B: Thank you. I'll look it up.
expressions: I'm calling about — introducing the reason for a phone call

challenge.cue: You've reached the wrong branch.
challenge.model: Sorry about that. I'm trying to contact the branch on Lake Road.
challenge.followUp: Do you have their number?

items.title: A bad connection
items.cue: Practise this situation: A bad connection. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Sorry, you're breaking up.
B: Can you hear me now?
A: A little better, but I missed the last sentence.
B: I'll move closer to the window.
A: Thanks. That's much clearer.
B: Great. I'll repeat what I said.
expressions: you're breaking up — the call audio keeps cutting out

challenge.cue: The connection is still poor.
challenge.model: I'm still having trouble hearing you.
challenge.followUp: Could we continue by message instead?

items.title: Taking a message
items.cue: Practise this situation: Taking a message. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hello, could I speak to Priya, please?
B: She's in a meeting. Can I take a message?
A: Yes, please tell her Max called about Friday's booking.
B: Certainly. Does she have your number?
A: Yes, but I can leave it again.
B: That would be helpful, thank you.
expressions: Can I take a message? — offering to pass information to someone

challenge.cue: Could you spell your name?
challenge.model: Of course. It's Max, M-A-X.
challenge.followUp: Could you read the message back to me?

items.title: Following up on a message
items.cue: Practise this situation: Following up on a message. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hi, just following up on my message about lunch.
B: Sorry, I saw it but forgot to reply.
A: No worries. Are you free tomorrow?
B: Yes, after one.
A: Great. Shall we meet at the café downstairs?
B: Sounds good. See you there.
expressions: just following up — politely returning to an earlier message

challenge.cue: I haven't seen your message.
challenge.model: No problem. I was asking whether you're free for lunch.
challenge.followUp: Would tomorrow after one suit you?

items.title: Checking message tone
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking message tone. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Does this message sound too direct?
B: Which part are you worried about?
A: The sentence that says, 'Send it today.'
B: You could say, 'Could you send it today, please?'
A: That sounds better. Thanks.
B: You can also explain why you need it.
expressions: Which part are you worried about? — asking what specifically concerns someone

challenge.cue: It needs to sound urgent.
challenge.model: Then keep the deadline clear and add a short reason.
challenge.followUp: Could you say you need it for tomorrow's meeting?

items.title: Ending a call
items.cue: Practise this situation: Ending a call. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I think that covers everything.
B: Great. I'll email the details shortly.
A: Thanks for your help today.
B: You're welcome.
A: Have a good afternoon.
B: You too. Goodbye.
expressions: That covers everything — all the necessary points have been discussed

challenge.cue: Before you go, one more thing.
challenge.model: Of course. I've got another minute.
challenge.followUp: What else would you like to check?

items.title: Asking for the Wi-Fi password
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking for the Wi-Fi password. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could you tell me the Wi-Fi password?
B: It's written on the card by the counter.
A: Thanks. Is that a capital B?
B: Yes, the first letter is a capital.
A: Great. I'm connected now.
B: Glad it worked.
expressions: I'm connected — my device has joined the network

challenge.cue: It says the password is incorrect.
challenge.model: I may have typed it wrong. I'll check it again.
challenge.followUp: Is the last character a zero or the letter O?

items.title: Trouble opening a file
items.cue: Practise this situation: Trouble opening a file. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I can't open the file you sent.
B: What happens when you try?
A: It says the format isn't supported.
B: I'll send a PDF version.
A: Thanks. That should be easier to open.
B: Let me know if it works.
expressions: What happens when you try? — asking for a description of a problem

challenge.cue: I don't have a PDF version.
challenge.model: That's okay. We can try another format.
challenge.followUp: Could you paste the text into a message?

items.title: Finding a button
items.cue: Practise this situation: Finding a button. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'm trying to change my profile picture.
B: Open your profile and look for Edit.
A: Okay, I've found it.
B: Now select the picture icon.
A: Got it. I can choose a new photo.
B: That's right. Save it when you're done.
expressions: I've found it — I have located it

challenge.cue: My screen doesn't have an Edit button.
challenge.model: Okay, your version may be different.
challenge.followUp: What buttons can you see on the profile page?

items.title: Sharing a screen
items.cue: Practise this situation: Sharing a screen. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Can you see my screen?
B: Not yet. I can only see your camera.
A: Let me try sharing again.
B: Okay, I can see it now.
A: Great. I'll open the document.
B: The text is a little small. Could you zoom in?
expressions: Could you zoom in? — Could you make the display larger?

challenge.cue: You're sharing the wrong window.
challenge.model: Thanks for letting me know. I'll switch to the document.
challenge.followUp: Can you see the correct window now?

items.title: A device is not charging
items.cue: Practise this situation: A device is not charging. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: My phone doesn't seem to be charging.
B: Have you tried a different cable?
A: Not yet. Do you have one I could try?
B: Yes, here you go.
A: Thanks. I'll see whether that helps.
B: Let me know what happens.
expressions: doesn't seem to be — appears not to be

challenge.cue: The other cable doesn't work either.
challenge.model: Then I'm not sure what the problem is.
challenge.followUp: Could you help me find a repair service?

items.title: Asking before posting a photo
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking before posting a photo. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I took a nice photo of us yesterday.
B: Oh, can I see it?
A: Of course. Are you okay with me posting it?
B: I'd rather you didn't post that one.
A: No problem. I'll keep it private.
B: Thanks for asking first.
expressions: I'd rather you didn't — expressing a preference that someone not do something

challenge.cue: You can post it, but please don't tag me.
challenge.model: Sure. I'll leave your name out.
challenge.followUp: Would you like me to send you a copy?

items.title: Asking someone to repeat
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking someone to repeat. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Sorry, could you say that again?
B: Of course. I asked what time you finish work.
A: Oh, I usually finish at six.
B: Do you go straight home afterwards?
A: Most days, yes. Sometimes I meet a friend.
B: That sounds nice.
expressions: Could you say that again? — asking for repetition

challenge.cue: Which part did you miss?
challenge.model: I heard the beginning, but I missed the time you mentioned.
challenge.followUp: Could you repeat just the last part?

items.title: Checking a word's meaning
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking a word's meaning. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: What does 'roughly' mean here?
B: It means 'approximately'.
A: So 'roughly ten minutes' isn't exactly ten?
B: That's right. It could be a little more or less.
A: Got it. Thanks for explaining.
B: You're welcome.
expressions: Got it — I understand

challenge.cue: Can you use it in your own sentence?
challenge.model: Sure. It takes roughly twenty minutes to walk to work.
challenge.followUp: Does that sound natural?

items.title: Practising with a partner
items.cue: Practise this situation: Practising with a partner. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Would you like to practise English together?
B: Sure. What should we talk about?
A: Let's pretend we're ordering food.
B: Okay. I'll be the waiter first.
A: Great. After that, we can switch roles.
B: Sounds good. Ready?
expressions: switch roles — exchange the parts each person plays

challenge.cue: I get nervous when I make mistakes.
challenge.model: That's okay. We can keep the first round short.
challenge.followUp: Would you like to read an example together first?

items.title: Requesting useful correction
items.cue: Practise this situation: Requesting useful correction. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could you listen to my short answer?
B: Of course. Do you want corrections as you speak?
A: Could you wait until I finish?
B: Sure. I'll make a few notes.
A: Thanks. Please focus on one or two useful changes.
B: Okay. Go ahead when you're ready.
expressions: focus on — give most attention to

challenge.cue: There are quite a few things we could change.
challenge.model: Let's choose the two that would make my meaning clearest.
challenge.followUp: Which change should I practise first?

items.title: Describing a forgotten word
items.cue: Practise this situation: Describing a forgotten word. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I can't remember the English word for it.
B: Can you describe what it does?
A: It's the thing you use to open a tin.
B: Do you mean a tin opener?
A: Yes, that's it!
B: You're welcome. Describing it worked well.
expressions: the thing you use to — describing an object by its purpose

challenge.cue: Do you mean the tool with two handles?
challenge.model: Yes, it has two handles and a small wheel.
challenge.followUp: What do you call that tool?

items.title: Making a realistic practice plan
items.cue: Practise this situation: Making a realistic practice plan. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: How much English practice are you doing?
B: About ten minutes after dinner.
A: That sounds manageable. What do you do?
B: I read a short conversation and then change the details.
A: Do you record yourself too?
B: Sometimes. It helps me notice where I stop.
expressions: That sounds manageable — that seems possible to handle

challenge.cue: I missed practice all week.
challenge.model: You can start again with a short conversation today.
challenge.followUp: Which topic would feel easiest to begin with?

items.title: Talking about a new hobby
items.cue: Practise this situation: Talking about a new hobby. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I've started learning to draw.
B: Really? What made you choose that?
A: I wanted something relaxing to do after work.
B: Are you taking a class?
A: I'm using a beginner's book for now.
B: I'd love to see your drawings sometime.
expressions: for now — at the present time, possibly temporarily

challenge.cue: I'm not very good at it yet.
challenge.model: That's normal when you're starting. I'm still learning too.
challenge.followUp: What do you enjoy drawing most?

items.title: Discussing a film
items.cue: Practise this situation: Discussing a film. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Have you seen that new comedy?
B: Yes, I watched it last weekend.
A: What did you think of it?
B: The first half was funny, but the ending felt rushed.
A: That's useful to know. I might still watch it.
B: Let me know what you think.
expressions: What did you think of it? — asking for someone's opinion

challenge.cue: I loved the ending, actually.
challenge.model: That's interesting. We noticed different things.
challenge.followUp: What did you like about it?

items.title: Joining an exercise class
items.cue: Practise this situation: Joining an exercise class. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Is this class suitable for beginners?
B: Yes, the instructor offers easier options.
A: Good. I haven't done this before.
B: You can go at your own pace.
A: That makes me feel better.
B: Just let the instructor know it's your first class.
expressions: go at your own pace — proceed at a speed comfortable for you

challenge.cue: The beginner class is in the other room.
challenge.model: Thanks for telling me. I must have come to the wrong room.
challenge.followUp: Could you show me where it is?

items.title: Recommending a book
items.cue: Practise this situation: Recommending a book. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'm looking for something interesting to read.
B: What kind of books do you usually enjoy?
A: Stories with short chapters.
B: You might like this collection of short stories.
A: Thanks. Is the language difficult?
B: It's fairly simple, though there are a few new words.
expressions: You might like — a gentle suggestion based on someone's interests

challenge.cue: I've already read that one.
challenge.model: Oh, I see. I'll think of another suggestion.
challenge.followUp: What did you enjoy about it?

items.title: Talking about cooking
items.cue: Practise this situation: Talking about cooking. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I tried making bread yesterday.
B: How did it turn out?
A: A little heavy, but it tasted good.
B: That's a good start.
A: Next time I'll give it more time to rise.
B: Let me know how the next one goes.
expressions: How did it turn out? — What was the result?

challenge.cue: Mine didn't work at all.
challenge.model: That's disappointing after all that effort.
challenge.followUp: What happened when you baked it?

items.title: Choosing a weekend activity
items.cue: Practise this situation: Choosing a weekend activity. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Do you fancy doing something this weekend?
B: Yes, but I'd prefer something inexpensive.
A: We could go for a walk and bring lunch.
B: That sounds ideal.
A: Shall we try the park near the river?
B: Yes, I've been meaning to go there.
expressions: I've been meaning to — I have intended to do something for some time

challenge.cue: I don't feel like walking much.
challenge.model: No problem. We could sit somewhere outdoors instead.
challenge.followUp: Would you like to have a picnic?

items.title: Responding to good news
items.cue: Practise this situation: Responding to good news. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I got the job I applied for!
B: That's great news! Congratulations.
A: Thanks. I'm excited and a bit nervous.
B: That makes sense. It's a big change.
A: I start next month.
B: What are you most looking forward to?
expressions: looking forward to — feeling pleased about something in the future

challenge.cue: I'm worried I won't be good enough.
challenge.model: It sounds like you're putting a lot of pressure on yourself.
challenge.followUp: What would help you feel more prepared?

items.title: Listening after a difficult day
items.cue: Practise this situation: Listening after a difficult day. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: You seem a bit quiet today.
B: It's been a difficult day at work.
A: I'm sorry to hear that. Want to talk about it?
B: Maybe later. I need a little time first.
A: Of course. I'm here if you want to talk.
B: Thanks. I appreciate that.
expressions: I'm here if you want to talk — offering support without pressure

challenge.cue: I don't want advice. I just need to talk.
challenge.model: Of course. I'll listen.
challenge.followUp: Would you like to tell me what happened?

items.title: Checking in with a friend
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking in with a friend. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Hey, we haven't spoken for a while.
B: I know. Things have been busy.
A: How have you been doing?
B: I'm okay, just a little tired.
A: Would you like to catch up over coffee?
B: I'd like that. Maybe on Sunday.
expressions: catch up — talk and exchange recent news

challenge.cue: I don't have much energy for going out.
challenge.model: That's okay. We can keep it simple.
challenge.followUp: Would a short phone call be easier?

items.title: Making a small apology
items.cue: Practise this situation: Making a small apology. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'm sorry I forgot to reply yesterday.
B: It's okay. I wondered if you were busy.
A: I was, but I should have sent a quick message.
B: Thanks for saying that.
A: I've checked the dates now. Saturday works for me.
B: Great. Let's confirm it.
expressions: Thanks for saying that — appreciating someone's words or acknowledgement

challenge.cue: I felt a bit ignored, to be honest.
challenge.model: I'm sorry. I can understand why it felt that way.
challenge.followUp: Would you like to talk about it?

items.title: Thanking someone specifically
items.cue: Practise this situation: Thanking someone specifically. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Thanks for helping me move yesterday.
B: You're welcome. I'm glad I could help.
A: Carrying those boxes would have taken me all day.
B: We got it done pretty quickly together.
A: Let me buy you lunch sometime.
B: That would be lovely.
expressions: return the favour — help someone who previously helped you

challenge.cue: You don't need to buy me anything.
challenge.model: Okay. I just wanted you to know how much it helped.
challenge.followUp: Can I return the favour sometime?

items.title: Responding to a disappointment
items.cue: Practise this situation: Responding to a disappointment. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: My weekend trip has been cancelled.
B: Oh, that's disappointing.
A: Yes, I was really looking forward to it.
B: I can imagine. Do you have another plan?
A: Not yet. I might have a quiet weekend instead.
B: That sounds reasonable.
expressions: I can imagine — showing that you can understand a feeling

challenge.cue: Everyone keeps telling me to look on the bright side.
challenge.model: That sounds frustrating when you're still disappointed.
challenge.followUp: Would you rather talk about the trip or something else?

items.title: Saying no to extra work
items.cue: Practise this situation: Saying no to extra work. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Could you take on another task today?
B: I can't finish another one today, I'm afraid.
A: What are you working on?
B: The two reports due this afternoon.
A: Okay. Let's review the priorities.
B: Thanks. I could start something new tomorrow.
expressions: take on — accept responsibility for additional work

challenge.cue: It really needs to be done today.
challenge.model: Then we'll need to move one of my current deadlines.
challenge.followUp: Which task should I put aside?

items.title: Keeping personal information private
items.cue: Practise this situation: Keeping personal information private. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: How much do you earn?
B: I'd rather keep that private.
A: Oh, sorry. I didn't mean to pry.
B: No worries. I'm happy to talk about the job itself.
A: Sure. Are you enjoying it?
B: Yes, especially the people I work with.
expressions: I'd rather keep that private — I prefer not to share that information

challenge.cue: I'm only curious.
challenge.model: I understand, but I'd still rather not share that.
challenge.followUp: What would you like to know about the work itself?

items.title: Asking before borrowing
items.cue: Practise this situation: Asking before borrowing. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Is that my notebook?
B: Yes, I borrowed it for a moment.
A: Please ask me before taking it next time.
B: Sorry. I should have checked.
A: Thanks. I use it for personal notes.
B: I understand. Here it is.
expressions: Please ask me before — setting a clear expectation

challenge.cue: I only used one blank page.
challenge.model: I understand, but I still need you to ask first.
challenge.followUp: Could you use the spare notebook next time?

items.title: Suggesting a different restaurant
items.cue: Practise this situation: Suggesting a different restaurant. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Shall we go to the expensive place again?
B: I'd prefer somewhere a little cheaper tonight.
A: Sure. Do you have anywhere in mind?
B: There's a small noodle shop nearby.
A: That sounds good to me.
B: Great. I'll check whether it's open.
expressions: Do you have anywhere in mind? — Have you thought of a particular place?

challenge.cue: It's a special occasion, though.
challenge.model: I know, and I'd still like to celebrate. That restaurant is beyond my budget tonight.
challenge.followUp: Could we choose somewhere less expensive?

items.title: Protecting quiet time
items.cue: Practise this situation: Protecting quiet time. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Can I call you later tonight?
B: Could we talk tomorrow instead?
A: Sure. Is everything okay?
B: Yes, I just need an evening without calls.
A: Of course. What time tomorrow?
B: After lunch would be good.
expressions: tonight doesn't work for me — I am unavailable or unwilling tonight

challenge.cue: It'll only take a few minutes.
challenge.model: I understand, but tonight doesn't work for me.
challenge.followUp: Could you send a message if it's something simple?

items.title: Declining food politely
items.cue: Practise this situation: Declining food politely. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Would you like another serving?
B: It was delicious, but I'm full, thank you.
A: Are you sure? There's plenty left.
B: I'm sure. I really enjoyed it.
A: Okay. Would you like some water?
B: Yes, please. That would be lovely.
expressions: I've had enough — I do not want or need any more

challenge.cue: Just a little more!
challenge.model: Thank you, but I've had enough. It was a lovely meal.
challenge.followUp: Could I help clear the table instead?

items.title: Correcting a time
items.cue: Practise this situation: Correcting a time. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I'll meet you at fifteen past six.
B: Do you mean quarter past six?
A: Yes, six fifteen. Sorry, I said that awkwardly.
B: No problem. I just wanted to check.
A: Thanks. Let's meet at the entrance.
B: See you there.
expressions: I just wanted to check — explaining why you asked for confirmation

challenge.cue: I heard six fifty.
challenge.model: Thanks for checking. I mean six fifteen, one-five.
challenge.followUp: Does that time still work for you?

items.title: Explaining a different meaning
items.cue: Practise this situation: Explaining a different meaning. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: You said the meeting was off.
B: I meant the timing was wrong, not that it was cancelled.
A: Oh, I misunderstood.
B: Sorry, I wasn't clear. It's still happening at three.
A: Thanks for explaining.
B: I'll send the correct time to everyone.
expressions: Sorry, I wasn't clear — taking responsibility for unclear wording

challenge.cue: So should I still attend?
challenge.model: Yes, please come. The meeting is still happening.
challenge.followUp: Can you make it at three?

items.title: Correcting a person's assumption
items.cue: Practise this situation: Correcting a person's assumption. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: You work from home every day, right?
B: Not every day. I go into the office twice a week.
A: Oh, I thought you were fully remote.
B: I used to be, but that changed recently.
A: Which days do you go in?
B: Usually Tuesday and Thursday.
expressions: Not every day — politely correcting an overgeneralisation

challenge.cue: I thought you said you never went in.
challenge.model: I did work from home all week before. My arrangement changed last month.
challenge.followUp: Would you like me to check which days I'll be in next week?

items.title: Buying time to explain
items.cue: Practise this situation: Buying time to explain. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Why did you choose that course?
B: Let me think how to explain it.
A: Take your time.
B: I wanted something practical that I could use at work.
A: So the job connection mattered most?
B: Yes, that's the main reason.
expressions: Let me think how to explain it — asking for a moment to organise your thoughts

challenge.cue: Do you mean it was required for your job?
challenge.model: No, it wasn't required. I chose it because I thought it would be useful.
challenge.followUp: Does that make sense?

items.title: Checking a number
items.cue: Practise this situation: Checking a number. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: Did you say thirteen or thirty?
B: Thirty, three-zero.
A: Thanks. I sometimes mix those up.
B: No problem. I'll write it down.
A: That's helpful. So we need thirty copies.
B: Exactly.
expressions: I sometimes mix those up — I sometimes confuse those things

challenge.cue: Actually, I said thirteen.
challenge.model: Thanks for correcting me. Thirteen, one-three.
challenge.followUp: Could you write the number down too?

items.title: Restating an idea simply
items.cue: Practise this situation: Restating an idea simply. Respond to the other person and keep the conversation going.
items.model:
A: I don't think I explained my idea well.
B: Could you put it another way?
A: Sure. Let's do a small version first and see what happens.
B: Oh, you mean try it before doing the whole thing?
A: Exactly. Then we can decide what to change.
B: That makes sense.
expressions: Could you put it another way? — asking for a different explanation

challenge.cue: I'm still not sure what we'd do first.
challenge.model: The first step would be to try it with five people.
challenge.followUp: Would a concrete example help?

items.title: Sentence building: Meeting people
items.cue: Meet someone at a class. Find one interest you share without looking at the examples.
items.model:
I used to work in a shop, but now I work in an office.

I used to live with my parents, but now I share a flat.

I used to drive to work, but now I take the train.
expressions: I used to ..., but now ...
items.note: Use used to + base verb for a past state or habit that has changed.

tasks.tight: Replace the old and current situation with two true details about yourself.
tasks.loose: Introduce yourself, explain one change in your life and ask the other person a question.
tasks.free: Meet someone at a class. Find one interest you share without looking at the examples.

items.title: Sentence building: Small talk
items.cue: Talk about your week for one minute, then imagine and answer a follow-up question.
items.model:
I've been cooking more lately.

I've been quite busy lately.

I've been spending more time outdoors lately.
expressions: I've been ... lately.
items.note: Use an -ing verb for an ongoing recent activity, or an adjective after been for a state.

tasks.tight: Replace the activity or feeling with something true about your recent life.
tasks.loose: Give a short update, add one detail and ask about the other person's week.
tasks.free: Talk about your week for one minute, then imagine and answer a follow-up question.

items.title: Sentence building: Making plans
items.cue: Plan a day out together. Change one part of the plan when the weather changes.
items.model:
Would Saturday morning work for you?

Would a video call work for you?

Would a café near the station work for you?
expressions: Would ... work for you?
items.note: The subject can be a time, place or arrangement. Work means be suitable here.

tasks.tight: Make three suggestions: a time, a way to meet and a place.
tasks.loose: Arrange a meeting. Offer two times, reject one politely and confirm the final plan.
tasks.free: Plan a day out together. Change one part of the plan when the weather changes.

items.title: Sentence building: Requests and help
