items.cue: Solve a practical problem with another person. Ask for only the help you actually need.
items.model:
Could you hold the door, please?

Could you send me the address, please?

Could you check the spelling, please?
expressions: Could you ... , please?
items.note: Use the base verb after could you: send, not sent or sending.

tasks.tight: Replace the action with three small favours you might ask for.
tasks.loose: Ask for help, explain why and respond when the person has only five minutes.
tasks.free: Solve a practical problem with another person. Ask for only the help you actually need.

items.title: Sentence building: Food and cafés
items.cue: Order for yourself when your first choice is unavailable. Choose an alternative.
items.model:
Could I have a glass of water, please?

Could I have the dressing on the side, please?

Could I have a few more minutes, please?
expressions: Could I have ... , please?
items.note: Could I have is a polite request. Use a/an for one countable item where needed.

tasks.tight: Change the requested item once, then make a request that is not about food.
tasks.loose: Order a meal, ask one question about it and politely correct a mistake.
tasks.free: Order for yourself when your first choice is unavailable. Choose an alternative.

items.title: Sentence building: Shopping
items.cue: Choose something within a budget. Leave without buying if nothing suits you.
items.model:
Do you have this in a larger size?

Do you have this in green?

Do you have this in a different material?
expressions: Do you have this in ...?
items.note: This can refer to an item you are pointing at. In introduces a version or option.

tasks.tight: Ask about size, colour and material for an item you would actually buy.
tasks.loose: Compare two items, state a preference and explain one reason.
tasks.free: Choose something within a budget. Leave without buying if nothing suits you.

items.title: Sentence building: Money and services
items.cue: Call about an unclear bill. Keep asking questions until you can summarise the explanation.
items.model:
Could you explain this service charge?

Could you explain the difference between these plans?

Could you explain how the cancellation works?
expressions: Could you explain ...?
items.note: Explain takes a direct object: explain the fee to me, not explain me the fee.

tasks.tight: Choose a charge, an option and a process you want explained.
tasks.loose: Ask about a service, check the cost and confirm what happens next.
tasks.free: Call about an unclear bill. Keep asking questions until you can summarise the explanation.

items.title: Sentence building: Getting around
items.cue: Find another way to reach your destination after a route change.
items.model:
Does this bus go to the city centre?

Does this train go to the airport?

Does this road go to the beach?
expressions: Does this ... go to ...?
items.note: Use go, not goes, after does. Adapt the verb when asking a different kind of question.

tasks.tight: Replace the transport or route and the destination with local examples.
tasks.loose: Ask about a route, check where to get off and repeat the directions back.
tasks.free: Find another way to reach your destination after a route change.

items.title: Sentence building: Travel and hotels
items.cue: Explain a room problem and agree on a practical next step.
items.model:
Is it possible to leave our bags here?

Is it possible to check in early?

Is it possible to move to a quieter room?
expressions: Is it possible to ...?
items.note: Use to + base verb. A request may be declined; practise a calm alternative.

tasks.tight: Make three realistic hotel requests using the same opening.
tasks.loose: Check in, ask about one service and handle a request that cannot be met.
tasks.free: Explain a room problem and agree on a practical next step.

items.title: Sentence building: Home and neighbours
items.cue: Agree on housework with someone who has a different schedule from yours.
items.model:
Could we make a cleaning schedule?

Could we keep the hallway clear?

Could we agree on a quieter time?
expressions: Could we ...?
items.note: We includes the speaker and invites a shared solution.

tasks.tight: Suggest three arrangements that would make shared living easier.
tasks.loose: Describe a small household problem and suggest a fair arrangement.
tasks.free: Agree on housework with someone who has a different schedule from yours.

items.title: Sentence building: Appointments
items.cue: Reschedule an appointment while working around a busy week.
items.model:
I'd like to book an appointment.

I'd like to change the time.

I'd like to check what I need to bring.
expressions: I'd like to ...
items.note: I'd is I would. Use to + base verb after would like.

tasks.tight: Change the verb phrase to fit three appointment tasks.
tasks.loose: Book a time, confirm the date and ask what to bring.
tasks.free: Reschedule an appointment while working around a busy week.

items.title: Sentence building: Work updates
items.cue: Tell a colleague what is done, what remains and when you expect to finish.
items.model:
I've finished the draft, but I still need to check the figures.

I've finished packing, but I still need to print the label.

I've finished the slides, but I still need to practise the talk.
expressions: I've finished ..., but I still need to ...
items.note: After finished, use a noun or an -ing form. After need to, use the base verb.

tasks.tight: Name a completed part and a remaining part of one real task.
tasks.loose: Give an update, explain a delay and ask which unfinished part matters most.
tasks.free: Tell a colleague what is done, what remains and when you expect to finish.

items.title: Sentence building: Meetings
items.cue: Choose between two plans with another person. Reach a decision without using the sample frame.
items.model:
I see your point, but we haven't checked the dates.

I see your point, but the room may be too small.

I see your point, but I'd like to hear another option.
expressions: I see your point, but ...
items.note: Follow but with a complete clause. Keep the concern specific rather than criticising the person.

tasks.tight: Keep the acknowledgement and change the concern three times.
tasks.loose: Discuss a plan, disagree about one detail and suggest a workable alternative.
tasks.free: Choose between two plans with another person. Reach a decision without using the sample frame.

items.title: Sentence building: Phone and messages
items.cue: Make an enquiry when the first person cannot help and transfers your call.
items.model:
I'm calling about my appointment tomorrow.

I'm calling about the parcel that hasn't arrived.

I'm calling about the email you sent yesterday.
expressions: I'm calling about ...
items.note: About is followed by a noun phrase or an -ing form, not a bare verb.

tasks.tight: Replace the reason for calling with three realistic situations.
tasks.loose: Start a call, explain the reason, check one detail and close politely.
tasks.free: Make an enquiry when the first person cannot help and transfers your call.

items.title: Sentence building: Technology
items.cue: Describe a technology problem to someone who cannot see your screen.
items.model:
When I open the file, I get an error message.

When I tap Save, nothing happens.

When I plug in the charger, the light flashes.
expressions: When I ..., ...
items.note: Report what you observe. Do not guess the cause if you do not know it.

tasks.tight: Describe an action and the visible result for three device problems.
tasks.loose: Explain a problem, answer a clarifying question and report what happens after trying a suggestion.
tasks.free: Describe a technology problem to someone who cannot see your screen.

items.title: Sentence building: Learning English
items.cue: Continue a conversation even when you miss a word. Use a description or clarification.
items.model:
Do you mean the meeting starts at ten?

Do you mean I should bring the original document?

Do you mean the shop is closed all day?
expressions: Do you mean ...?
items.note: Mean can be followed by a noun phrase or a clause. Your intonation can invite confirmation.

tasks.tight: Choose three things a listener might need to confirm.
tasks.loose: Ask for repetition, check your interpretation and respond to the actual meaning.
tasks.free: Continue a conversation even when you miss a word. Use a description or clarification.

items.title: Sentence building: Hobbies and free time
items.cue: Choose a free-time activity with someone whose preferences differ from yours.
items.model:
I've been meaning to try that café.

I've been meaning to read that book.

I've been meaning to join a walking group.
expressions: I've been meaning to ...
items.note: This describes an intention you have had for some time, often something not done yet.

tasks.tight: Replace the activity with three things you have wanted to do.
tasks.loose: Talk about a hobby, explain why it interests you and make a small plan.
tasks.free: Choose a free-time activity with someone whose preferences differ from yours.

items.title: Sentence building: Friends and feelings
items.cue: Respond to good or disappointing news. Let the other person decide how much to share.
items.model:
Would you like to talk about it?

Would you like some company?

Would you like me to call you tomorrow?
expressions: Would you like ...?
items.note: Use a noun, to + verb, or me to + verb. Accept no without pressure.

tasks.tight: Offer a conversation, company and a practical action in your own words.
tasks.loose: Listen to a friend's update and offer one kind of support without insisting.
tasks.free: Respond to good or disappointing news. Let the other person decide how much to share.

items.title: Sentence building: Boundaries and choices
items.cue: Handle a repeated invitation that you cannot accept. Stay clear and polite.
items.model:
I'd rather stay home tonight.

I'd rather keep that private.

I'd rather choose a less expensive place.
expressions: I'd rather ...
items.note: Use the base verb after I'd rather when the subject stays the same: I'd rather go.

tasks.tight: State three real preferences politely and give a reason only if you want to.
tasks.loose: Decline a request, repeat your boundary once and offer an alternative if appropriate.
tasks.free: Handle a repeated invitation that you cannot accept. Stay clear and polite.

items.title: Sentence building: Repairing misunderstandings
items.cue: Resolve a misunderstanding about a time, number or responsibility without reading a script.
items.model:
What I meant was that we need more time.

What I meant was that the room is small, not that it's unpleasant.

What I meant was that I can help tomorrow.
expressions: What I meant was ...
items.note: That can introduce the clarification. Keep the second explanation simpler than the first.

tasks.tight: Clarify three ideas using a short complete clause after was.
tasks.loose: Explain an idea, notice a misunderstanding and restate the meaning simply.
tasks.free: Resolve a misunderstanding about a time, number or responsibility without reading a script.

resources.title: 1. Choose one situation
resources.body: Filter Conversations by a topic you need soon. Six situations are available for each of 20 topics. The IDs connect the conversations, challenges and your notes.

resources.title: 2. Tight practice
resources.body: Read the six lines aloud as both A and B. Repeat any difficult line slowly. Change one or two details, such as the time, item or place. Use the matching Sentence builder pattern for more examples.

resources.title: 3. Loose practice
resources.body: Look only at the situation and useful expression. Make a new six-turn conversation using your own details. Keep the meaning clear; the wording can change.

resources.title: 4. Free practice
resources.body: Close or cover the model. Imagine a real conversation for 30–60 seconds. Respond to what the other person says rather than forcing a memorised expression into every turn.

resources.title: 5. Try the unexpected reply
resources.body: Open Reply challenges for the same ID. Read column C and reply aloud before looking at E. Write your reply in amber column D. Column F offers a follow-up question; use it only if it fits.

resources.title: 6. Record and review
resources.body: Optional: record yourself on your own device. Listen once, choose one useful improvement and try again. Use My practice to record true details, your stage and a review date. The workbook does not record audio.

resources.title: A manageable starting session
resources.body: Try one conversation and its challenge for about 10–15 minutes. Repeat it on another day with different details. This is a large reference library, not a requirement to finish a fixed number every day.

resources.title: How this fits the other books
resources.body: Use the 600-chunk workbook to find language you need. Use Big 30 to build longer personal answers. Use this workbook to practise the back-and-forth: listening to a cue, responding, clarifying and continuing.

resources.title: The examples are flexible
resources.body: The dialogues and replies are new fictional learning examples. There is more than one good reply. Adapt names, details and preferences to your own life. Any prices, availability or service policies are fictional scenario details.

resources.title: Solo or with a partner
resources.body: Solo: read one role, pause, then answer as the other person. With a partner: swap A and B, then introduce the unexpected reply. This workbook contains written models, not audio or pronunciation scoring.

resources.title: Optional role-play prompt
resources.body: Act as my English conversation partner. Ask me which situation from this workbook I want to practise and whether I want an easy or more challenging conversation. Then play the other person and send only one short turn at a time. Wait for my reply before continuing. Use natural everyday English. After a few turns, introduce one realistic change or misunderstanding. Do not write my answers for me unless I ask. At the end, give me up to three useful corrections, a natural version of my own wording and two follow-up questions. Keep feedback kind and specific. If I type "help", give me one short hint. I will paste the situation and any expressions I want to practise next.
